marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q016.takeaway: Vaginal lining is non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q016.displayText: The lining epithelium of the vagina is non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium. Other sites lined by non-keratinised squamous epithelium include the mouth, tongue, pharynx, esophagus and cornea. Keratinised stratified squamous epithelium covers the skin of the whole body and forms the epidermis. The source image shows a histological section of vaginal epithelium with superficial, intermediate, parabasal and basal layers.
emphasis: mouth, tongue, pharynx, esophagus and cornea

rationales.a: The vagina has a true stratified squamous lining, not a pseudostratified columnar epithelium.
rationales.b: Vaginal squamous epithelium is non-keratinized; keratinized stratified squamous describes epidermis.
rationales.d: The vaginal lining is stratified squamous, not pseudostratified columnar.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q017.takeaway: Transitional epithelium lines the urinary bladder and can flatten as the bladder stretches.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q017.displayText: The image shows transitional epithelium and is seen in the urinary bladder. The deepest layer has columnar cells, the middle layers are polyhedral, and the surface layer has large, characteristic umbrella cells. Transitional epithelium is found in the renal pelvis and calyces, ureter, urinary bladder and part of the urethra, hence the term urothelium. In the urinary bladder it can stretch considerably without being damaged; when stretched, it appears thinner and the cells become flattened or rounded.

rationales.a: Bile ducts are not lined by urothelium; transitional epithelium lines the urinary tract.
rationales.b: The common bile duct is part of the biliary tract and does not have transitional lining.
rationales.c: Skin is covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, not transitional epithelium.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q018.takeaway: The ureter has transitional epithelium over a thick fibroelastic lamina propria, with smooth muscle and outer adventitia.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q018.displayText: The histological section is of the ureter. The image shows a thick fibroelastic lamina propria underneath stratified transitional epithelium. There are no mucosal or submucosal glands and no submucosa. A layer of smooth muscle is present outside the mucosa, and the outer adventitial layer contains fibroelastic connective tissue with blood vessels, lymphatics and nerves. The source includes a labelled cross-section of ureter showing transitional epithelium, lumen, smooth muscle and adventitia.

rationales.a: The female urethra is not a ureter; its lining and wall do not show the ureter’s transitional mucosa with prominent outer adventitia.
rationales.b: Male urethra has regionally changing epithelial lining and is not the transitional-lined ureter shown.
rationales.d: Vas deferens has a pseudostratified columnar lining and a prominent muscular wall, unlike the transitional-lined ureter.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q019.takeaway: Sertoli (sustentacular) cells are epithelial support cells that surround developing germ cells in seminiferous tubules.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q019.displayText: Sertoli cells, also called sustentacular cells, are the epithelial supporting cells of the seminiferous tubules. They are derived from the epithelial sex cords of the developing gonads. They are tall simple columnar cells that surround proliferating and differentiating germ cells, forming pockets around them. Sertoli cells provide nutrients and phagocytose excess cytoplasm from newly forming spermatozoa. The source includes a section of seminiferous ducts illustrating the different cell types.

rationales.a: Germ cells are the developing spermatogenic cells; Sertoli cells provide epithelial support.
rationales.b: Leydig cells lie in interstitial tissue and produce testosterone, rather than supporting seminiferous epithelium.
rationales.d: Peritubular cells surround tubules externally; Sertoli cells are the epithelial supporting cells within the seminiferous tubules.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q020.takeaway: Vas deferens has pseudostratified columnar epithelium and a prominent three-layered muscular wall.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q020.displayText: Among the given options the histological section is most likely vas deferens or ductus deferens. Its epithelium is pseudostratified columnar and it is surrounded by a prominent muscular layer. This muscular layer contains inner and outer longitudinal muscle and a middle circular layer. An adventitia of connective tissue surrounds the muscularis layer. The ductus deferens extends from the epididymis to the ejaculatory ducts.

rationales.a: The ureter has transitional epithelium and a different muscular arrangement; the shown duct has pseudostratified lining and a thick three-layered muscularis.
rationales.b: The epididymis has pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia, but not the prominent vas-deferens muscular wall.
rationales.c: Seminal vesicle has a folded glandular mucosa; the source-described duct with a prominent muscular layer is vas deferens.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q021.takeaway: Glycogen in glandular epithelial cells and secretory-phase endometrial layers identify uterine endometrium.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q021.displayText: Among the given options, the histological image is most likely endometrium. It shows glycogen masses in the basal cytoplasm of epithelial cells lining glands, a feature of the early secretory phase of the endometrium. The uterus has an outer smooth-muscle myometrium and an inner endometrium. The endometrium has three layers: stratum compactum, stratum spongiosum (together forming the stratum functionalis), and stratum basalis. During the menstrual cycle the endometrium progressively thickens, uterine glands grow in length and become tortuous/saw-toothed during the secretory phase, and glandular epithelium changes from cuboidal to columnar with glycogen vacuoles.

rationales.a: Seminiferous tubules contain spermatogenic cells and Sertoli cells, not endometrial glands with glycogen in the basal epithelial cytoplasm.
rationales.b: Prostate is a male gland and does not have the cyclic endometrial layers and secretory-phase glands described.
rationales.d: Mammary gland is not the uterine lining; the described glycogen masses and compactum/spongiosum/basalis layers identify endometrium.

marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q022.takeaway: Epididymal stereocilia are long microvilli, so the epididymis is the exception to sites with motile cilia.
marrow__ANAT_CH15_Q022.displayText: The arrow marks cilia. All the structures listed in the options have ciliated lining epithelium except the epididymis, which is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia. The source image is a histological section of epididymis showing pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia. Cilia are minute hair-like projections, while stereocilia are very long, thick microvilli. Ciliated columnar epithelium occurs in much of the respiratory tract, uterus and uterine tube, efferent ductules of the testis, parts of the middle ear and auditory tube, ependymal lining, central canal of the spinal cord and ventricles of the brain. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium is seen in the trachea and large bronchi.

rationales.a: Oviduct is lined by ciliated epithelium that helps move the ovum.
rationales.c: Bronchial respiratory epithelium has motile cilia that move mucus.
rationales.d: Ependyma has ciliated lining in the ventricles/central canal; epididymis has stereocilia, which are microvilli.
